cta.title: Discover your learning style
cta.description: Answer 15 quick questions (VARK model) and the AI will start generating modules adapted to the way you learn best.

intro.title: What is your learning style?
intro.description: The VARK model identifies how you prefer to absorb information: Visual, Auditory, Reading/Writing or Kinesthetic. It's 15 multiple-choice questions — about 5 minutes. The result personalizes the modules generated by the AI.

q1.text: When you need to learn a new subject, you prefer to:

options.visual: See diagrams, charts, mind maps or videos about the topic.
options.auditory: Listen to a detailed explanation or discuss the subject with someone.
options.reading_writing: Read texts, articles or books about the subject.
options.kinesthetic: Try it out in practice or apply the knowledge in real situations.

q2.text: When receiving instructions to assemble a new piece of equipment, you prefer to:

options.visual: See pictures or watch a demonstration video.
options.auditory: Listen to someone explaining step by step how to do it.
options.reading_writing: Read the instruction manual in detail.
options.kinesthetic: Try assembling it by trial and error, handling the parts.

q3.text: When you are learning a new software or app, you usually:

options.visual: Pay attention to the visual elements of the interface and icons.
options.auditory: Prefer narrated tutorials or verbal explanations.
options.reading_writing: Look for written guides or detailed documentation.
options.kinesthetic: Explore the software by clicking different options to see what happens.

q4.text: In a class or lecture, you feel most engaged when:

options.visual: The presenter uses visual aids like slides, charts or videos.
options.auditory: There are discussions, Q&A sessions or debates.
options.reading_writing: Detailed written materials are provided to follow along.
options.kinesthetic: There are hands-on activities or interactive demonstrations.

q5.text: When you need to memorize information for an exam, you usually:

options.visual: Create mind maps, use different colors or visualize the information.
options.auditory: Repeat the information out loud or explain it to someone else.
options.reading_writing: Take detailed notes and reread them several times.
options.kinesthetic: Link the information to practical examples or create physical mnemonics.

q6.text: When learning a new skill (like playing an instrument or practicing a sport), you:

options.visual: Carefully watch someone demonstrating the correct technique.
options.auditory: Listen to detailed explanations about how to perform the movements.
options.reading_writing: Read about techniques, strategies and the theory behind the practice.
options.kinesthetic: Try doing it yourself, adjusting your technique as you practice.

q7.text: When you are lost in an unfamiliar place, you prefer to:

options.visual: Look at a map or use an app with visual GPS.
options.auditory: Ask someone for directions or use the GPS voice commands.
options.kinesthetic: Explore the area until you find the right way.

q8.text: When learning a new language, you find it most effective to:

options.visual: Use picture flashcards, watch movies or videos in the language.
options.auditory: Talk with native speakers or listen to audio and podcasts.
options.reading_writing: Study grammar, vocabulary and do written exercises.
options.kinesthetic: Practice in real situations or through interactive games.

q9.text: When you need to explain something complex to someone, you tend to:

options.visual: Draw diagrams or use objects to illustrate.
options.auditory: Explain verbally with details and analogies.
options.reading_writing: Write a detailed explanation or provide written references.
options.kinesthetic: Demonstrate in practice or guide the person through an experience.

q10.text: In a teamwork environment, you prefer to:

options.visual: Use visual boards, charts or presentations to communicate ideas.
options.auditory: Take part in brainstorming meetings and group discussions.
options.reading_writing: Prepare written documents, reports or detailed emails.
options.kinesthetic: Build prototypes, models or practical demonstrations.

q11.text: When choosing an online course, you feel most attracted to:

options.visual: Courses with lots of visual resources, videos and infographics.
options.auditory: Live webinars, podcasts or classes with discussions.
options.reading_writing: Courses based on texts, articles and reading materials.
options.kinesthetic: Courses with practical projects, simulations or interactive exercises.

q12.text: When you are cooking a new recipe, you prefer to:

options.visual: See photos of the process or watch a video tutorial.
options.auditory: Listen to someone explaining how to make it or discuss the recipe.
options.reading_writing: Follow the written instructions step by step.
options.kinesthetic: Experiment with ingredients and techniques, adjusting as needed.

q13.text: When solving a complex problem, you usually:

options.visual: Create diagrams, flowcharts or visual maps of the problem.
options.auditory: Talk through the problem out loud or discuss it with other people.
options.reading_writing: List the pros and cons or write down your ideas in detail.
options.kinesthetic: Try different practical approaches to see what works.

q14.text: When you are learning about a historical event, you prefer to:

options.visual: Watch documentaries, visual timelines or reenactments.
options.auditory: Listen to podcasts, audiobooks or lectures on the topic.
options.reading_writing: Read history books, articles or original documents.
options.kinesthetic: Visit museums, historical sites or take part in reenactments.

q15.text: When receiving feedback about your work, you prefer to:

options.visual: See performance charts or visual examples of what to do.
options.auditory: Have a detailed conversation about your strengths and weaknesses.
options.reading_writing: Receive a written report with analysis and recommendations.
options.kinesthetic: Work alongside someone to improve through practice.

visual.name: Visual
visual.description: You learn best through visual resources like charts, diagrams, mind maps and videos. You easily remember what you see and prefer visually organized information.

auditory.name: Auditory
auditory.description: You learn best by listening and speaking, through discussions, podcasts and verbal explanations. You retain information better when you can hear it and talk it through.

reading_writing.name: Reading/Writing
reading_writing.description: You learn best through the written word, with books, articles and detailed notes. You easily absorb information presented in text format.

kinesthetic.name: Kinesthetic
kinesthetic.description: You learn best through practical experience, with hands-on activities and real applications. You retain knowledge better when you can experiment and apply what you are learning.

multimodal.name: Multimodal
multimodal.description: You have a flexible learning style, combining traits from multiple styles. This lets you adapt to different teaching methods and benefit from many kinds of educational resources.

visual.title: Use visual resources
visual.description: Incorporate mind maps, diagrams, charts and videos into your studies. Use different colors to highlight important information.

visual.title: Create visual representations
visual.description: Turn texts and concepts into visual representations like infographics, flowcharts or schematics.

visual.title: Organize visually
visual.description: Keep your study environment visually organized, with color codes and clear signage.

auditory.title: Learn by listening
auditory.description: Use podcasts, audiobooks and recorded lessons. Take part in group discussions and debates about the topics you study.

auditory.title: Verbalize knowledge
auditory.description: Read out loud, explain concepts to other people or record yourself explaining the content.

auditory.title: Use sound mnemonics
auditory.description: Create rhymes, songs or sound patterns to memorize important information.

reading_writing.title: Prioritize written materials
reading_writing.description: Use books, articles, handouts and other written materials. Take detailed notes during lessons.

reading_writing.title: Rewrite information
reading_writing.description: Rewrite important concepts in your own words to improve understanding and retention.

reading_writing.title: Organize in writing
reading_writing.description: Create lists, summaries and written outlines to structure your knowledge.

kinesthetic.title: Learn by doing
kinesthetic.description: Seek out practical activities, experiments and real applications of knowledge. Take part in simulations and role-playing.

kinesthetic.title: Move while studying
kinesthetic.description: Walk while reading or reviewing content. Use gestures to link physical movements to important concepts.

kinesthetic.title: Build physical models
kinesthetic.description: Build models, mock-ups or physical representations of the concepts you are studying.

multimodal.title: Combine different approaches
multimodal.description: Alternate between study methods, combining visual, auditory, reading/writing and kinesthetic elements.

multimodal.title: Identify specific contexts
multimodal.description: Notice which styles work best for different kinds of content or learning situations.

multimodal.title: Create multisensory experiences
multimodal.description: Design activities that stimulate multiple senses at once to maximize retention.

result.title: Your dominant style is
result.multimodalNote: There was a tie between styles — your profile is multimodal. We saved "{{style}}" as your dominant style to personalize the AI, but you benefit from combining approaches.
result.aiNote: From now on, AI-generated modules will be adapted to your learning style.
